posts.altText: Static post headed “Doing more. Still overlooked?” It addresses being trusted with tasks but not decisions, suggests explaining a choice and its cost, and invites applications to Proving Ground.
posts.caption:
More completed tasks show that you can execute. They don't always show how you make a difficult call.

For your next recommendation, write three short sentences:
• I would choose this option.
• The cost or risk I accept is this.
• I would reconsider if this changed.

Fill in the specifics. That makes your reasoning easier to examine than a confident answer alone.

In Proving Ground, decision practice is marked against a visible standard. Each score explains what a top mark requires and where your answer fell short. Use that feedback to spot what your next recommendation needs.
posts.emotion: Inferred: frustration at being valued for execution but overlooked for responsibility, alongside a desire to earn trust in one's judgement.

Doing the task and choosing the task are different kinds of work.

For the hypothetical demand surge above, a useful answer names your priority, the cost you're accepting and what would make you reconsider. The point isn't to sound certain. It's to make your reasoning clear enough to examine.

Proving Ground shows the standard beside each score, so you can see what a top mark requires and where your answer fell short.
